on Thursday announced a financing agreement worth up to $47M with privately held AvenCell Therapeutics to help advance AvenCell’s pipeline of CAR-T cell therapies.
Cambridge, Massachusetts-based AvenCell's lead asset is AVC-201, an anti-CD123 CAR-T undergoing a Phase 1b expansion trial in relapsed/refractory acute myeloid leukemia.
As part of the deal, Ligand
has committed up to $41M across four tranches to fund AvenCell's pipeline assets, including AVC-201, in exchange for mid-single-digit to low-double-digit royalties on their future annual net sales.

While the first tranche is due when the deal closes, the rest will depend on several clinical milestones and specific financing conditions. The company also said it will separately disclose details of a Series C financing initiative worth up to $6M

title: Ligand, AvenCell ink financing deal worth up to $47M for CAR-T therapies
